title: Father used to teach Urdu
scope: The past imperfective (बोलता था, बोलती थीं) and the routine imperfective; कोई and कुछ as pronouns, adjectives and adverbs, oblique किसी, कोई + number, phrases (हर कोई, सब कुछ, कोई न कोई, कुछ और); चाहिए “is needed” with को and its past; की ज़रूरत है; ordinal numbers (पहला … दसवाँ, -वाँ); aggregatives (दोनों, तीनों, सैकड़ों); conjunct verbs with करना and होना (शुरू करना/होना, बंद करना/होना)

skills.kisi: कोई, कुछ and किसी with nouns

vocab.en: to go for a walk, trip

items.q: Fill the gap: “My grandmother used to chat with the children in the evening.”
items.hi: मेरी दादी जी शाम को बच्चों के साथ गपशप करती ___ ।
items.say: मेरी दादी जी शाम को बच्चों के साथ गपशप करती थीं ।
items.en: My[0] grandmother[1+2] {used to}[10] chat[8+9] with[6+7] the children[5] {in the evening}[3+4].
wrong: थे
थे is masculine. दादी is feminine: करती थीं.
था
था is masculine singular. A respected woman takes the feminine plural थीं.
items.why: The past imperfective is the participle + था, थी, थे, थीं. Respect makes the auxiliary plural: दादी जी … करती थीं.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Raj used to get up to a lot of mischief as a child.”
items.hi: राज बचपन में बहुत शरारत ___ था ।
items.say: राज बचपन में बहुत शरारत करता था ।
items.en: Raj[0] {used to}[6] {get up to}[5] {a lot of}[3] mischief[4] {as a child}[1+2].
wrong: करती
करती is feminine. Raj is a boy.
करते
करते is plural. Raj, spoken of plainly, is one person, as था shows.
items.why: The participle agrees with the subject, and था follows it.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Where did you use to work before? (to a man)”
items.hi: तुम पहले कहाँ काम करते ___ ?
items.say: तुम पहले कहाँ काम करते थे ?
items.en: Where[2] {did you use to}[0+5] work[3+4] before[1]? (to a man)
wrong: था
था is singular. तुम always takes plural agreement: करते थे.
थीं is feminine plural, but the participle करते is masculine. The auxiliary agrees with the participle: -tā था, -tī थी, -te थे, and -tī थीं for feminine plural.
items.why: तुम … करते थे to a man; a woman would be asked तुम … करती थीं.

items.q: Put this into the past (“used to …”)
items.a: मेरी बहिनें सुबह जल्दी उठती थीं ।
wrong: मेरी बहिनें सुबह जल्दी उठतीं थीं ।
Only the auxiliary carries the plural nasal: उठती थीं, just as उठती हैं. The participle is nasalized only when the auxiliary is dropped.
मेरी बहिनें सुबह जल्दी उठती थी ।
थी is singular. बहिनें is plural: थीं.
items.why: Replace हैं with थीं. The participle stays the same.
items.hi: मेरी बहिनें सुबह जल्दी उठती हैं ।
items.say: मेरी बहिनें सुबह जल्दी उठती थीं ।
items.en: My[0] sisters[1] {used to}[5] {get up}[4] early[3] {in the morning}[2].

items.q: Fill the gap: “In that village girls didn't use to go to school.”
items.hi: उस गाँव में लड़कियाँ स्कूल नहीं ___ थीं ।
items.say: उस गाँव में लड़कियाँ स्कूल नहीं जाती थीं ।
items.en: In[2] that[0] village[1] girls[3] {didn't use to}[5+7] go[6] {to school}[4].
wrong: जातीं
With थीं present the participle is not nasalized: जाती थीं. The nasal moves to the participle only when the auxiliary is dropped.
जाते
जाते is masculine. लड़कियाँ are feminine.
items.why: Feminine plural: -tī + थीं.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My mother used to know Sanskrit.”
items.hi: मेरी माँ को संस्कृत आती ___ ।
items.say: मेरी माँ को संस्कृत आती थी ।
items.en: My[0] mother[1] {used to know}[2+4+5] Sanskrit[3].
wrong: The verb agrees with संस्कृत, the subject of the को construction, not with माँ. संस्कृत is singular: थी.
था
था is masculine. संस्कृत is feminine.
items.why: X को (language) आना in the past: आती थी, agreeing with the language.

items.q: Fill the gap: “As children we used to play all day.”
items.hi: बचपन में हम दिन भर ___ थे ।
items.say: बचपन में हम दिन भर खेलते थे ।
items.en: {As children}[0+1] we[2] {used to}[6] play[5] {all day}[3+4].
wrong: खेलता
खेलता is singular. हम is plural: खेलते थे.
खेलना
खेलना is the infinitive. The tense uses the participle, stem + -tā, -tī, -te.
items.why: हम takes the -te participle and थे.

items.q: There is no auxiliary here. What does the sentence mean?
items.a: In the summer we would stay in the mountains.
wrong: In the summer we stay in the mountains.
A present statement keeps हैं, which is dropped only after नहीं. With no auxiliary at all, the verb tells of a past routine: “we would …”.
Last summer we stayed in the mountains.
A single past event needs the perfective, taught in Unit 11. The imperfective tells of a habit.
items.why: The ‘routine imperfective’: the participle alone narrates past habits, like English “would”.
items.hi: गर्मियों में हम पहाड़ों पर रहते ।
items.say: गर्मियों में हम पहाड़ों पर रहते ।
items.en: {In the summer}[0+1] we[2] {would stay}[5] in[4] the mountains[3].

items.q: Fill the gap: “In the past the air in this city used to be clean.”
items.hi: पहले इस शहर में हवा साफ़ ___ थी ।
items.say: पहले इस शहर में हवा साफ़ होती थी ।
items.en: {In the past}[0] the air[4] in[3] this[1] city[2] {used to be}[6+7] clean[5].
wrong: होता
होता is masculine. हवा is feminine.
होते
होते is masculine plural. हवा is feminine singular.
items.why: होता था and होती थी mean “used to be”, for lasting states in the past.

items.q: Which means “My brother used to work in Delhi”?
items.a: मेरा भाई दिल्ली में काम करता था ।
wrong: मेरा भाई दिल्ली में काम करता है ।
करता है is present: “works”. “Used to” needs था.
मेरा भाई दिल्ली में काम करते थे ।
करते थे is plural. With मेरा the brother is spoken of plainly, so करता था.
items.why: Participle + था gives करता था “used to do”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Those people didn't use to eat rice.”
items.hi: वे लोग चावल नहीं ___ थे ।
items.say: वे लोग चावल नहीं खाते थे ।
items.en: Those[0] people[1] {didn't use to}[3+5] eat[4] rice[2].
wrong: खाता
खाता is singular. लोग is plural.
खाती
खाती is feminine. लोग takes the masculine plural.
items.why: नहीं goes before the participle: नहीं खाते थे.

items.q: Fill the gap: “There is someone at the door.”
items.hi: दरवाज़े पर ___ है ।
items.say: दरवाज़े पर कोई है ।
items.en: {There is}[3] someone[2] at[1] the door[0].
wrong: कुछ
कुछ as a pronoun means “something”. For a person, कोई.
किसी
किसी is the oblique of कोई, used before a postposition. Here कोई is the subject.
items.why: As pronouns, कोई “someone” is for people and कुछ “something” for things.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan knows nothing.”
items.hi: मोहन ___ नहीं जानता ।
items.say: मोहन कुछ नहीं जानता ।
items.en: Mohan[0] knows[3] nothing[1+2].
wrong: कोई
कोई नहीं means “nobody”. “Nothing” is कुछ नहीं.
किसी
किसी is the oblique of कोई, which is for people. “Nothing” is कुछ नहीं.
items.why: कुछ नहीं “nothing”, कोई नहीं “nobody”; the two words may stand apart.

items.q: Which means “everyone”?
wrong: कोई न कोई
कोई न कोई means “someone or other”.
सब कुछ
सब कुछ means “everything”.
items.why: हर “each, every” + कोई “someone”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Everyone here speaks Hindi.”
items.hi: यहाँ ___ हिन्दी बोलता है ।
items.say: यहाँ हर कोई हिन्दी बोलता है ।
items.en: Everyone[1+2] here[0] speaks[4+5] Hindi[3].
wrong: सब कुछ
सब कुछ is “everything”, for things. For people, हर कोई.
कुछ न कुछ
कुछ न कुछ means “something or other”.
items.why: हर कोई takes a singular verb: हर कोई … बोलता है.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My mother knows everything.”
items.say: मेरी माँ सब कुछ जानती हैं ।
items.en: My[0] mother[1] knows[4+5] everything[2+3].
wrong: हर कोई
हर कोई means “everyone”.
कुछ न कुछ
कुछ न कुछ means “something or other”.
items.why: सब कुछ “everything”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Bring some more milk.”
items.hi: ___ और दूध लाओ ।
items.say: कुछ और दूध लाओ ।
items.en: Bring[3] some[0] more[1] milk[2].
wrong: कोई
कोई और means “someone else”. With a substance like milk, कुछ और “some more”.
हर
हर means “every”, and goes with a singular countable noun.
items.why: कुछ और “something else, some more”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “This isn't my bicycle; it's someone else's.”
items.hi: यह मेरी साइकिल नहीं है, ___ और की है ।
items.say: यह मेरी साइकिल नहीं है, किसी और की है ।
items.en: This[0] isn't[3+4] my[1] bicycle[2]; it's[8] {someone else's}[5+6+7].
wrong: कोई
Before the postposition की, कोई becomes the oblique किसी, as in किसी और की.
किस
किस is the oblique of कौन “who?”. किस की would ask “whose?”.
items.why: कोई और “someone else”; oblique किसी और.

lessons.title: किसी, कुछ, हर
lessons.desc: Some, about, rather; the oblique किसी

items.q: Fill the gap: “There is some letter on the table.”
items.hi: मेज़ पर ___ चिट्ठी है ।
items.say: मेज़ पर कोई चिट्ठी है ।
items.en: {There is}[4] some[2] letter[3] on[1] the table[0].
wrong: कुछ
With a single countable item, “some” is कोई. कुछ goes with plurals and with substances.
किसी
किसी is the oblique form, used before a postposition. Here the noun is direct.
items.why: कोई + singular noun: “some, a certain”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Do you know a good doctor?”
items.hi: क्या आप ___ अच्छे डाक्टर को जानते हैं ?
items.say: क्या आप किसी अच्छे डाक्टर को जानते हैं ?
items.en: Do[7] you[1] know[5+6] a[2] good[3] doctor[4]?
wrong: कोई
The noun is followed by को, so कोई becomes the oblique किसी.
किस
किस is the oblique of कौन. किस अच्छे डाक्टर को would mean “which good doctor?”.
items.why: The oblique of कोई is किसी, both as pronoun and as adjective.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Some girls play in the garden.”
items.hi: ___ लड़कियाँ बग़ीचे में खेलती हैं ।
items.say: कुछ लड़कियाँ बग़ीचे में खेलती हैं ।
items.en: Some[0] girls[1] play[4+5] in[3] the garden[2].
wrong: कोई
In the plural, कोई changes to कुछ, as in कुछ लड़कियाँ.
किसी
किसी is the singular oblique. The plural of कोई is कुछ.
items.why: कोई लड़की, but कुछ लड़कियाँ.

items.q: Fill the gap: “In the evening I teach Sanskrit to some students.”
items.hi: शाम को मैं ___ विद्यार्थियों को संस्कृत पढ़ाता हूँ ।
items.say: शाम को मैं कुछ विद्यार्थियों को संस्कृत पढ़ाता हूँ ।
items.en: {In the evening}[0+1] I[2] teach[7+8] Sanskrit[6] to[5] some[3] students[4].
wrong: किसी
किसी is singular. In the plural, कोई and किसी both become कुछ, as in कुछ विद्यार्थियों को.
किन
किन is the plural oblique of कौन “who?”, not of कोई.
items.why: कुछ stays the same before a postposition: कुछ लड़कों के लिए.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita brings some daal from the market.”
items.hi: सीता बाज़ार से ___ दाल लाती है ।
items.say: सीता बाज़ार से कुछ दाल लाती है ।
items.en: Sita[0] brings[5+6] some[3] daal[4] from[2] the market[1].
wrong: कोई
कोई goes with a single countable item. With a substance like daal, “some” is कुछ.
किसी
किसी is the oblique of कोई, and there is no postposition after दाल.
items.why: कुछ goes with substances, as in कुछ दूध, कुछ पैसा.

items.q: Fill the gap: “This room is a bit small.”
items.hi: यह कमरा ___ छोटा है ।
items.say: यह कमरा कुछ छोटा है ।
items.en: This[0] room[1] is[4] {a bit}[2] small[3].
wrong: कोई
कोई is not used as an adverb. Before an adjective, “rather, a bit” is कुछ.
कई
कई means “several” and goes with plural nouns.
items.why: कुछ before an adjective means “rather, somewhat”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “There were about a hundred guests in the hotel last night.”
items.hi: कल रात होटल में ___ सौ मेहमान थे ।
items.say: कल रात होटल में कोई सौ मेहमान थे ।
items.en: {There were}[7] about[4] {a hundred}[5] guests[6] in[3] the hotel[2] {last night}[0+1].
wrong: हर
हर means “every”. Before a number, “about” is कोई.
किसी
Before a number कोई means “about” and never becomes किसी.
items.why: कोई + number: “about, approximately”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I have been ill for about ten days.”
items.hi: मैं ___ दस दिन से बीमार हूँ ।
items.say: मैं कोई दस दिन से बीमार हूँ ।
items.en: I[0] {have been}[6] ill[5] for[4] about[1] ten[2] days[3].
wrong: किसी
Before a number, कोई means “about” and stays कोई even before a postposition such as से.
कुछ
Before a number, “about” is कोई.
items.why: Compare कोई पाँच दिन में “in about five days”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Which city do you live in? (to a man)”
items.hi: आप ___ शहर में रहते हैं ?
items.say: आप किस शहर में रहते हैं ?
items.en: {Which city}[1+2] do you[0] live[4+5] in[3]? (to a man)
wrong: किसी
किसी शहर में means “in some city”. To ask “which?”, use किस, the oblique of कौन.
कौनसा
Before में, कौनसा becomes oblique: कौनसे.
items.why: Don't confuse किसी (oblique of कोई) with किस (oblique of कौन).

items.q: Fill the gap: “There is a fan in every room.”
items.hi: ___ कमरे में एक पंखा है ।
items.say: हर कमरे में एक पंखा है ।
items.en: {There is}[5] a[3] fan[4] in[2] every[0] room[1].
wrong: सब
सब means “all” and goes with a plural: सब कमरों में. With a singular noun, “every” is हर.
कुछ
कुछ कमरे would be “some rooms”, and they would be plural and oblique: कुछ कमरों में.
items.why: हर “each, every” + a singular noun.

lessons.title: चाहिए
lessons.desc: Needs and wants; की ज़रूरत है

items.q: Fill the gap: “I need a warm blanket.”
items.hi: ___ एक गरम कंबल चाहिए ।
items.say: मुझे एक गरम कंबल चाहिए ।
items.en: I[0] need[4] a[1] warm[2] blanket[3].
wrong: With चाहिए the person who needs takes को, giving मुझे (= मुझ को).
मेरा
मेरा means “my”. The person who needs takes को, giving मुझे.
items.why: चाहिए “is needed”: the person takes को, the thing is the subject.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The guests needed more samosas.”
items.hi: मेहमानों को और समोसे चाहिए ___ ।
items.say: मेहमानों को और समोसे चाहिए थे ।
items.en: {The guests}[0+1] needed[4+5] more[2] samosas[3].
wrong: था
था is singular. With चाहिए the thing needed is the subject, and the auxiliary agrees with it, not with the person who takes को. समोसे is plural.
थीं is feminine. समोसा is masculine.
items.why: For the past, add था, थी, थे, थीं to चाहिए.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Raj needed a new book.”
items.hi: राज को एक नई किताब चाहिए ___ ।
items.say: राज को एक नई किताब चाहिए थी ।
items.en: Raj[0] needed[1+5+6] a[2] new[3] book[4].
wrong: था
Raj is a man, but With चाहिए the thing needed is the subject, and the auxiliary agrees with it, not with the person who takes को. किताब is feminine: थी.
थीं is plural. There is one book.
items.why: चाहिए थी agrees with किताब.

items.q: Fill the gap: “This child needs a doctor.”
items.hi: इस बच्चे को डाक्टर की ___ है ।
items.say: इस बच्चे को डाक्टर की ज़रूरत है ।
items.en: This[0] child[1] needs[2+4+5+6] a doctor[3].
wrong: ज़रूरी
ज़रूरी is the adjective “necessary”. “Need” is the noun ज़रूरत.
ज़रूर
ज़रूर means “of course, certainly”.
items.why: X को Y की ज़रूरत है “X needs Y”, literally “to X is a need of Y”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “We need a big room.”
items.hi: हमें एक बड़े कमरे ___ ज़रूरत है ।
items.say: हमें एक बड़े कमरे की ज़रूरत है ।
items.en: We[0] need[4+5+6] a[1] big[2] room[3].
wrong: का
ज़रूरत is feminine, so it is की ज़रूरत.
को
Only the person takes को. The thing needed is linked by की.
items.why: ज़रूरत is a feminine noun: की ज़रूरत.

items.q: Say the same with ज़रूरत
items.a: मोहन को चप्पलों की ज़रूरत है ।
wrong: मोहन को चप्पलें की ज़रूरत है ।
Before की the noun is oblique: चप्पलों.
मोहन को चप्पलों का ज़रूरत है ।
ज़रूरत is feminine, so की, not का.
items.why: The thing needed becomes oblique before की ज़रूरत.
items.hi: मोहन को चप्पलें चाहिए ।
items.say: मोहन को चप्पलों की ज़रूरत है ।
items.en: Mohan[0] needs[1+3+4+5] sandals[2].

items.q: Fill the gap: “Does anyone want tea?”
items.hi: क्या ___ को चाय चाहिए ?
items.say: क्या किसी को चाय चाहिए ?
items.en: Does anyone[1+2] want[4] tea[3]?
wrong: कोई
Before को, कोई becomes the oblique किसी.
किस
किस को चाय चाहिए ? asks “who wants tea?”. With क्या, a yes/no question, it is किसी.
items.why: किसी को “to anyone”.

items.q: Which means “Nobody needs this old car”?
items.a: किसी को यह पुरानी गाड़ी नहीं चाहिए ।
wrong: कोई को यह पुरानी गाड़ी नहीं चाहिए ।
Before को, कोई becomes किसी.
कोई यह पुरानी गाड़ी नहीं चाहिए ।
The person who needs must take को, as in किसी को.
items.why: किसी को … नहीं चाहिए “nobody needs”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My daughter studies in the fifth class.”
items.hi: मेरी बेटी ___ क्लास में पढ़ती है ।
items.say: मेरी बेटी पाँचवीं क्लास में पढ़ती है ।
items.en: My[0] daughter[1] studies[5+6] in[4] the fifth[2] class[3].
wrong: पाँचवाँ
पाँचवाँ is masculine. क्लास is feminine: पाँचवीं.
पाँचवें
पाँचवें is masculine plural or oblique. क्लास is feminine: पाँचवीं.
items.why: Ordinals inflect like adjectives, with nasal endings: पाँचवाँ, पाँचवीं, पाँचवें.

items.q: Fill the gap: “This is my third question.”
items.hi: यह मेरा ___ सवाल है ।
items.say: यह मेरा तीसरा सवाल है ।
items.en: This[0] is[4] my[1] third[2] question[3].
wrong: तीनवाँ
Not a word: “first” to “fourth” (and “sixth”) are irregular. “Third” is तीसरा.
तीसरी
तीसरी is feminine. सवाल is masculine.
items.why: पहला, दूसरा, तीसरा, चौथा, then पाँचवाँ, छठा, सातवाँ …

items.q: Fill the gap: “This is this year's first holiday.”
items.hi: यह इस साल की ___ छुट्टी है ।
items.say: यह इस साल की पहली छुट्टी है ।
items.en: This[0] is[6] this[1] year's[2+3] first[4] holiday[5].
wrong: पहला
पहला is masculine. छुट्टी is feminine.
पहले
पहले is masculine plural or oblique (and also the adverb “before”). छुट्टी is feminine.
items.why: पहला “first” agrees like an -ā adjective.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Grandmother lives with her (own) fourth son.”
items.hi: दादी जी अपने ___ बेटे के साथ रहती हैं ।
items.say: दादी जी अपने चौथे बेटे के साथ रहती हैं ।
items.en: Grandmother[0+1] lives[7+8] with[5+6] {her (own)}[2] fourth[3] son[4].
wrong: चौथा
Before के साथ, the ordinal is oblique like the noun: चौथे बेटे.
चारवाँ
Not a word: “fourth” is irregular, चौथा.
items.why: Ordinals take the oblique like other -ā adjectives.

items.q: Which word means “sixth”?
wrong: छहवाँ
Not a word. छठा is irregular, like पहला to चौथा.
छह
छह is “six”, the cardinal number.
items.why: छठा “sixth”, सातवाँ “seventh”.

items.q: बारह means “twelve”. What is “twelfth”?
wrong: बारहवा
The ending -vā̃ is nasal: बारहवाँ.
बारहों
The ending -õ makes an aggregative, बारहों “all twelve”.
items.why: From “fifth” on, add the nasal ending -vā̃ to the number.

items.q: Fill the gap: “All three brothers live in Delhi.”
items.hi: ___ भाई दिल्ली में रहते हैं ।
items.say: तीनों भाई दिल्ली में रहते हैं ।
items.en: {All three}[0] brothers[1] live[4+5] in[3] Delhi[2].
wrong: तीन
तीन is just “three”. “All three” is the aggregative तीनों.
तीसरे
तीसरे means “third”.
items.why: Aggregatives add -õ to the number: तीनों, चारों.

items.q: Fill the gap: “There were hundreds of people in that cinema.”
items.hi: उस सिनेमा में ___ लोग थे ।
items.say: उस सिनेमा में सैकड़ों लोग थे ।
items.en: {There were}[5] {hundreds of}[3] people[4] in[2] that[0] cinema[1].
wrong: सैकड़ा
सैकड़ा is “a hundred” as a noun. “Hundreds of” is the aggregative सैकड़ों.
सौ
सौ is “a hundred”. “Hundreds of” is सैकड़ों.
items.why: Aggregatives also give multiples: दर्जनों, सैकड़ों, हज़ारों.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Both children play in the garden.”
items.hi: ___ बच्चे बग़ीचे में खेलते हैं ।
items.say: दोनों बच्चे बग़ीचे में खेलते हैं ।
items.en: Both[0] children[1] play[4+5] in[3] the garden[2].
wrong: दोओं
Not a word: दोनों “both” is irregular.
दो
दो is just “two”. “Both” is दोनों.
items.why: दोनों is the irregular aggregative of दो.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Thousands of foreigners come to Varanasi every year.”
items.hi: हर साल ___ विदेशी वाराणसी आते हैं ।
items.say: हर साल हज़ारों विदेशी वाराणसी आते हैं ।
items.en: {Thousands of}[2] foreigners[3] come[5+6] to Varanasi[4] every[0] year[1].
wrong: हज़ार
हज़ार is “a thousand”. “Thousands of” is हज़ारों.
सैकड़ों
सैकड़ों means “hundreds of”.
items.why: हज़ार “thousand” → हज़ारों “thousands of”.

lessons.title: शुरू करना, शुरू होना
lessons.desc: Conjunct verbs with करना and होना

items.q: Fill the gap: “The post office closes at five o'clock.”
items.hi: डाकघर पाँच बजे बंद ___ है ।
items.say: डाकघर पाँच बजे बंद होता है ।
items.en: {The post office}[0] closes[3+4+5] {at five o'clock}[1+2].
wrong: करता
बंद करना needs an object: someone shuts something. Here the post office itself closes, so बंद होना.
होती
होती is feminine. डाकघर is masculine.
items.why: करना verbs are transitive; their होना partners are intransitive.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I start work at seven o'clock. (a man speaking)”
items.hi: मैं सात बजे काम शुरू ___ हूँ ।
items.say: मैं सात बजे काम शुरू करता हूँ ।
items.en: I[0] start[4+5+6] work[3] {at seven o'clock}[1+2]. (a man speaking)
wrong: होता
काम is the object here: I start it. That is शुरू करना.
करती
करती is feminine. The speaker is a man.
items.why: काम शुरू करना “to begin work”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “On Mondays my work starts early.”
items.hi: सोमवार को मेरा काम जल्दी शुरू ___ है ।
items.say: सोमवार को मेरा काम जल्दी शुरू होता है ।
items.en: {On Mondays}[0+1] my[2] work[3] starts[5+6+7] early[4].
wrong: करता
Nobody is doing the starting here. काम is the subject, so शुरू होना.
होती
होती is feminine. काम is masculine.
items.why: शुरू होना “to begin” has no object.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Pinki cleans her bicycle every Saturday.”
items.hi: पिंकी हर शनिवार को अपनी साइकिल ___ करती है ।
items.say: पिंकी हर शनिवार को अपनी साइकिल साफ़ करती है ।
items.en: Pinki[0] cleans[6+7+8] her[4] bicycle[5] every[1] Saturday[2+3].
wrong: ख़त्म
ख़त्म करना means “to finish”.
शुरू
शुरू करना means “to begin”.
items.why: साफ़ “clean” + करना “to clean”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan finishes his work at night.”
items.hi: मोहन रात को अपना काम ___ करता है ।
items.say: मोहन रात को अपना काम ख़त्म करता है ।
items.en: Mohan[0] finishes[5+6+7] his[3] work[4] {at night}[1+2].
wrong: शुरू
शुरू करना means “to begin”.
साफ़
साफ़ करना means “to clean”.
items.why: ख़त्म “finished” + करना “to finish”.

items.q: Which means “My holiday ends on Friday”?
items.a: मेरी छुट्टी शुक्रवार को ख़त्म होती है ।
wrong: मेरी छुट्टी शुक्रवार को ख़त्म करती है ।
करना would need someone who finishes something. The holiday itself ends: ख़त्म होना.
मेरी छुट्टी शुक्रवार को ख़त्म होता है ।
होता is masculine. छुट्टी is feminine.
items.why: The intransitive partner of ख़त्म करना is ख़त्म होना.

items.q: Fill the gap: “School used to start at eight o'clock in the past.”
items.hi: पहले स्कूल आठ बजे शुरू ___ था ।
items.say: पहले स्कूल आठ बजे शुरू होता था ।
items.en: School[1] {used to}[6] start[4+5] {at eight o'clock}[2+3] {in the past}[0].
wrong: करता
Here स्कूल is the subject and nothing is acted on, so शुरू होना.
होती
होती is feminine. स्कूल is masculine.
items.why: होता था is the past imperfective of शुरू होना.

items.en: Sita[0] {used to}[4] {go for a walk}[2+3] {in the morning}[1].
wrong: करता
करता is masculine. Sita is a woman.
थीं is plural. Sita, spoken of plainly, is one person.

items.en: Raj[0] needed[1+4+5] {a new}[2] table[3].
wrong: था
With चाहिए the auxiliary agrees with the thing needed, मेज़, which is feminine: थी.
नया
नया is masculine. मेज़ is feminine.

items.en: Someone[0] is[4] sitting[3] in[2] the garden[1].
wrong: कुछ
कुछ is “something”. For a person, कोई.
बैठे
बैठे is plural. कोई “someone” is singular.

items.en: Mohan[0] needs[1+3+4+5] rest[2].
wrong: का
ज़रूरत is feminine, so की ज़रूरत.
ज़रूरी
ज़रूरी is the adjective “necessary”. “Need” is the noun ज़रूरत.

items.en: {All four}[0] daughters[1] go[3+4] {to school}[2].
wrong: चार
चार बेटियाँ is just “four daughters”. “All four” is the aggregative चारों.
जाते
जाते is masculine. बेटियाँ is feminine.

items.en: My[0] first[1] teacher[2] was[4] {a Muslim}[3].
wrong: पहली
पहली is feminine. अध्यापक is masculine.
थी
थी is feminine. A respected teacher takes the masculine plural थे.
items.order: मेरे अध्यापक पहले मुसलमान थे would mean “My teacher was formerly a Muslim”, with पहले as the adverb “before”. As “first”, पहले goes before the noun.

items.en: That[0] shop[1] closes[4+5+6] {at seven o'clock}[2+3].
wrong: करती
बंद करना needs an object. The shop itself closes: बंद होना.
होता
होता is masculine. दुकान is feminine.

items.en: {The children}[0] {used to}[4] {get up}[3] early[2] {in the morning}[1].
wrong: उठता
उठता is singular. बच्चे is plural.
था
था is singular. बच्चे is plural: उठते थे.

items.en: These[0] shoes[1] are[4] {a bit}[2] big[3].
wrong: बड़ा
बड़ा is singular. जूते is plural.
कई
कई means “several” and goes before a plural noun. Before an adjective, “a bit” is कुछ.

items.en: Sita[0] needs[1+4] {a new}[2] sari[3].
wrong: नया
नया is masculine. साड़ी is feminine.
का
The person who needs takes को, not का, so it is सीता को.

items.en: {Lakhs of}[3] people[4] live[5+6] in[2] this[0] city[1].
wrong: लाख
लाख is “a lakh, a hundred thousand”. “Lakhs of” is the aggregative लाखों.
रहता
रहता is singular. लोग is plural.

items.en: Mohan[0] {used to know}[1+3+4] Gujarati[2].
wrong: आता
The verb agrees with गुजराती, which is feminine: आती.
थे
The verb agrees with गुजराती, which is singular: थी.

lessons.title: What does it mean?
lessons.desc: Read a sentence, pick the translation

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: बचपन में मैं रात को बहुत डरती थी ।
items.a: As a child I used to be very frightened at night.
wrong: As a child I was frightened one night.
A single event would need the perfective. डरती थी is a habit: “used to be frightened”.
I am very frightened at night.
थी puts it in the past, and बचपन में means “in childhood”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: शाम को घर में हमेशा कोई न कोई होता है ।
items.a: There is always someone or other at home in the evening.
wrong: There is nobody at home in the evening.
“Nobody” would be कोई नहीं.
Everyone is at home in the evening.
“Everyone” would be हर कोई.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: आज मौसम कुछ ठंडा है ।
items.a: The weather is rather cold today.
wrong: The weather is very cold today.
“Very” would be बहुत. कुछ before an adjective is “rather, a bit”.
Some weather is cold today.
कुछ before an adjective is an adverb: “rather”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: उसे कुछ और चाहिए था ।
wrong: He needed nothing else.
“Nothing” would be कुछ नहीं.
Someone else needed it.
“Someone else” would be कोई और. उसे is the person who needed.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: स्टेशन पर कोई पाँच विद्यार्थी बैठे थे ।
items.a: About five students were sitting at the station.
wrong: Five students were sitting at the station.
Before a number, कोई means “about”.
Some student was sitting at the station for five hours.
कोई before a number means “about”, and बैठे थे is plural.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मेरी तीसरी बहिन डाक्टर है ।
items.a: My third sister is a doctor.
wrong: My three sisters are doctors.
तीसरी is the ordinal “third”, and है is singular.
All three of my sisters are doctors.
“All three” would be the aggregative तीनों.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: दफ़्तर में हज़ारों चिट्ठियाँ आती थीं ।
items.a: Thousands of letters used to come to the office.
wrong: A thousand letters came to the office.
हज़ारों is “thousands of”, and आती थीं is a habit: “used to come”.
Thousands of letters come to the office.
थीं puts it in the past: “used to come”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मेरे भाई को नए जूते चाहिए थे ।
wrong: My brother had new shoes.
चाहिए means “is needed”. Having is not expressed this way.
My brother needs new shoes.
थे puts it in the past: “needed”.

items.q: Can the past imperfective translate “Yesterday I went to the market”?
items.a: No: a one-off past event needs the perfective, taught in Unit 11
wrong: Yes: it covers every past action
It always means “used to …”: habits and regular events.
Yes, as long as कल is added
कल does not change the meaning of the tense. A single event needs the perfective.
items.why: The past imperfective always has the sense “used to …”.

items.q: Which word is the grammatical subject of राज को नया थैला चाहिए ?
wrong: राज
A word followed by को is never the subject. Raj is the one who needs.
चाहिए
चाहिए is the verb, “is needed”.
items.why: The thing needed is the subject; that is why चाहिए था or थी agrees with it.

items.q: What is the difference between किसी and किस ?
items.a: किसी is the oblique of कोई “some(one)”; किस is the oblique of कौन “who?”
wrong: Both are obliques of कौन “who?”
Only किस is. किसी is the oblique of कोई, so किसी को is “to someone” and किस को “to whom?”.
किसी is singular and किस is plural
Both are singular. The plural obliques are कुछ (for कोई) and किन (for कौन).
items.why: किसी शहर में “in some city”, किस शहर में ? “in which city?”.

items.q: When does कोई stay कोई before a postposition?
items.a: When it means “about” before a number
wrong: When it refers to a thing
As an adjective it becomes किसी before a postposition, whatever the noun: किसी दुकान में.
Never: it always becomes किसी
Before a number it stays कोई, as in कोई दस दिन से.
items.why: कोई दस दिन से “for about ten days”.

items.q: What do कोई and किसी become in the plural?
items.a: कुछ, in both the direct and the oblique
wrong: किसी in the direct, कोई in the oblique
Both become कुछ, as in कुछ लड़के, कुछ लड़कों के लिए.
They stay कोई and किसी
कोई and किसी are singular. With plurals it is कुछ.
items.why: कई “several” is another plural partner of कोई.

items.q: Why is it बंद होती है in दुकान बंद होती है ?
items.a: The shop is the subject and nothing is acted on, so the intransitive होना is used
wrong: Because दुकान is feminine
Gender decides होती against होता, not होना against करना.
Because होती है describes a habit
Habits use the imperfective with both verbs: मोहन दुकान बंद करता है is also a habit.
items.why: करना verbs take an object (मोहन दुकान बंद करता है), but होना verbs do not.

items.q: How do ordinals such as पाँचवाँ agree?
items.a: Like -ā adjectives, with nasal endings: पाँचवीं, पाँचवें
wrong: They always stay पाँचवाँ
They agree with the noun: पाँचवीं क्लास, पाँचवें दिन.
Like -ā adjectives, without the nasal: पाँचवी, पाँचवे
The nasal stays in every form: पाँचवाँ, पाँचवीं, पाँचवें.
items.why: पहला, दूसरा, तीसरा, चौथा and छठा agree like ordinary -ā adjectives.
